checked_sources: Planar convex polygon disk-perimeter inequality and Cauchy Minkowski-perimeter additivity; reconstructed from mathematical definitions.
correctness.rationale: For every integer m>=3 and n>=2, each nonzero coefficient a_j induces the regular m-gon a_j conv(mu_m), and the Minkowski sum P has circumradius exactly R=max_{k in Z_m^n}|sum_j a_j omega^{k_j}| (vertices of convex hull of all phase sums). Cauchy planar perimeter additivity gives per(P)=2m sin(pi/m) sum_j|a_j|; the sum has at most mn edges. For a convex polygon with at most mn sides inscribed in a radius-R disk, per(P)<=2mn R sin(pi/(mn)), strict equality classification regular mn-gon. Equal amplitudes and coefficient phases 2pi(j-1)/(mn) modulo 2pi/m give exactly this polygon. Reverse equality rigidity forces mn distinct summand edge-direction classes and equal edge lengths, hence equal coefficient moduli and equally spaced phases up to permutation, one common phase, and independent mu_m factors. The proof handles all m,n in scope, vanishing coefficients (excluded at equality), support-one degeneracies, disk centers, and the n/m limits. Independent Git-tree object reconstruction yielded the supplied SHA-1; all seven original files inspected at source commit, including verbatim verify.py Git blob, which executed VERIFY_OK for 15 extremizer exhaustions and 960 random inequalities. Finite checks are corroborative only, not proofs of all-parameter statements.
residual_risks: The independent finite numerical checks use floating-point tolerances and do not certify the universal theorem; the analytic perimeter/rigidity argument carries that burden.
The source makes no claim for m=2, non-coordinate characters, dependent sets, or mixed root orders.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge pass for the exact m>=3 finite-order coordinate-character Sidon constant and all equality configurations, not a claim of inventing the polygon perimeter lemma. The strongest overlapping published Resultary finding proves the same type of geometric rigidity for the order-two Rademacher system only (n>=5); its signed-zonogon statement does not contain or logically imply the m>=3 regular-m-gon numeric formula without an additional finite-root geometric argument. Seigner 1997 proves the limiting order-two constant pi/2 using integration and coefficient phases; Hare-Ramsey prove qualitative epsilon-Kronecker-to-Sidon implications; Bourgain-Lewko prove structural Rademacher-Sidon and tensor/psi_2 Sidon theorems. Cartwright-Howlett-McMullen 1981 characterize endpoint values 1 and sqrt(sum d_pi^2), not this natural intermediate constant or extremizers. Searches of aliases, equal-root vector sums and polygon constructions found no independently covering m>=3 result. The formula is an elementary application of known sharp polygon geometry, a significant proximity/priority risk, so originality is best-of-knowledge only.
residual_risks: An unindexed older regular-polygon Minkowski sum theorem or independent finite-root Sidon theorem may give the identical formula/equality class under a different name.
The m=2 published sharp finite Rademacher result uses essentially the same perimeter/equality mechanism; the new scope is a natural exact m>=3 extension rather than a new general geometric principle.
Searches cannot certify worldwide priority, and comparisons are bounded to actually read sources.

value.rationale: The Fourier-analytic Sidon constant is a natural quantitative invariant for the independent coordinate characters of finite exponent, and the problem asks for its exact dependence on both torsion order m and finite cardinality n. The final answer includes a sharp closed expression for every m>=3,n>=2 and a COMPLETE rigid equality family (equal amplitudes, phases interlacing into a regular mn-gon). The result quantifies the finite-phase loss and its fixed-order asymptotic (pi/m)/sin(pi/m) and continuous-phase limit 1; it is not a sample-specific table. A future researcher working with finite torsion character sets could use this precise normalization and equality class; the source has a clear object and invariant motivation before computation. This is a modest natural exact invariant, not a new polygon theorem or broad Sidon classification. The proof uses standard geometry, which limits its depth but does not negate the exact structural fact.
residual_risks: The proof adapts classical disk-polygon perimeter and a published order-two strategy; value is exact natural finite-order Sidon data, not a new deep method.
No claims about m=2, unequal orders, general dependent finite sets, or an open general conjecture.
